transcript.content:
hi, i'm berry. i help people turn their dreams into pictures.

whenever you're ready, tell me your dream — however it comes back to you.
hey, that sounds cool. ok so i was on a streetcar just watching the conductor at first

something about watching them first, yeah.

what happened next?
i started noticing the lever he used when we went around bends. and then it felt like i was doing it with him, like i'd go through the motions of turning it and steering
that's strange, isn't it. one moment you're just watching and then somehow the steering's in you too.
yeah, it was weird. like i was in two places at once, watching and doing. but the next thing i knew i was on top of the car, only now it had turned into a train

the streetcar turning into a train while you're on top of it — that's a big jump.

how did it feel up there?
really high up, and the train was going fast. i nearly fell off a few times and i was scared

that rush of it, and trying to hold on. sounds like it had you properly scared.

were you alone on top of the train?
no, there was another family sitting up there with me. a small baby was there too, and it seemed thrilled with the ride
a small baby, happy up there while you were frightened. that contrast is odd.
yeah it felt like i was the only one who was scared. everyone else was just fine with it

being the only one scared, that can be its own lonely feeling.

what did you do then?
i was afraid i'd try to jump off, most of all when the train rounded a bend. i just kept trying to hold on

the bend being the worst of it, yeah. you said before the lever was for bends too.

so you stayed down and held on the whole time?
i think so, i don't remember exactly what happened next. just that the train was on a country road

on a country road, after all that speed. okay.

and how did things look from where you were?
everything below seemed far away. i mostly remember the rush and how high we were
that sense of height stayed with you, more than the ground itself.
yeah, the height and the speed. that's what really stuck with me

those two things, the height and the speed.

was there anything under the train, do you think, or was it just open country?
i don't remember seeing the tracks really, just that it was a country road. open country i guess

open country, no tracks you can recall.

could you feel the train moving when you held on, like the way it shook or shifted?
i don't remember the shaking exactly, just that it was fast and i had to hold on tight

fast, and you had to hold on. that's enough.

if you could pause the dream at one moment, the moment that stayed with you most, which would it be?
probably when we were rounding a bend and i was holding on, scared, while the baby was happy

the scared feeling and the happy baby, both at the same bend.

could you see the baby's face there, or just know it was happy?
i just knew it was happy. i don't remember its face

you just knew, that's how dreams do sometimes.

and the sky, when you picture that bend, do you see any of it?
i don't remember the sky at all. just the feeling of being up high

the height more than the look of it, right.

what was the scariest part about you nearly falling, do you remember?
just the idea of falling from that high up, with the train going that fast. and i kept thinking i might jump off

the falling, and also that worry you might jump. that's a different kind of fear.

was anyone else in the family noticing you were frightened, or were they in their own world?
i don't think they noticed me at all. they were in their own world

all around you, but not with you.

did you want them to notice?
i don't remember wanting them to. i just felt like i was the only one scared

you were on a streetcar, watching the conductor use the lever around bends, and then it felt like you were doing the steering too, watching and doing at the same time. next thing, you were on top of the car, only now it was a train, high up and going fast on a country road. a family was up there with you, and a small baby seemed thrilled, but you were the only one scared. you nearly fell a few times and kept thinking you might jump, especially on bends. you mostly remember the height and the speed, not really how anything looked, and you don't remember how it ended.

did i get that right? and was that where the dream ended, or did more happen after?
yeah that's right. that's where it ended for me

got it. i have your dream.

would you like to see it drawn?
yes, i would

there are a few ways i could draw it.

one is an old woodcut print, carved into hard lines, every shape bold and urgent. another is a dreamy charcoal drawing, smudged and blurred, caught in the motion of a speeding train. a third is a faded colour photograph, colours drained and muted, like a memory of fear on a bright day. and the fourth is a real-life photograph, as if seen through your eyes, vivid and immediate.

which feels closest to your dream, or would you describe your own way you'd like it drawn?
the dreamy charcoal one, definitely

i'll start with the conductor. just them on their own first — i picture them in a dark conductor's uniform, a cap, their back to you as they work the lever. some of this i'm filling in, these are my guesses.

does anything feel different about them, or would you leave them to me?
leave them to you, i don't remember what they looked like

okay, i'm sketching the conductor and the family and the small baby and the streetcar and the lever now — it'll appear on the right, and nothing else yet.

as for the top of the train, i picture the roof itself — dark, smooth, maybe slightly curved — and below it, the open country rolling past far down. i'm guessing at the roof and the country road, since you didn't see much. does any of that feel off, or would you leave the top of the train to me?
the roof and country feel right enough, go with your guess

okay, i'm sketching the top of the train now and it'll appear on the right. just that, nothing else is being drawn yet.

and i'll draw you too, since you're in the dream. how would you like to be drawn — as you are, if you want to tell me a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
however you imagine me is fine, i don't think i saw myself

i'll imagine you then, okay.

i'm sketching you now. everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can say if anything looks wrong once it's there.
i can see them. the conductor one looks right to me, and the one on top of the train with everyone up there too. the charcoal blur makes the speed feel real. i think it fits.

glad that feels right.

anything you'd like to tweak before i call it done?
no, it's good as it is.
then it's done. i hope it carries that height and speed for you.
thanks, it does. it's strange seeing it all laid out like that.
it can be, seeing it outside your head like that. sometimes that makes it land differently.
yeah, it does. it feels more real now, but in a good way.

that's good to hear. i'm glad it landed well.

take care of it, then.
i will, thanks berry
it was good doing this with you. hold onto that feeling — the dream's yours now.

turns.brief:
Move: retell. You have their dream as far as they've told it. Tell it back to them in a few plain sentences, in order and in their own words where you can: what happened, where, who was there, how it felt and how it looked. Add nothing they didn't say. Then ask whether you got it right, and whether that's where the dream ended or more happened after.
Ask nothing except what this move says.
